repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: No exact blocker; local JS/TS runtime and package-manager substrate.
repo_catalog.why: All-in-one toolkit with a Bun runtime, test runner, script runner, and Node.js-compatible package manager; good local execution substrate, but not agent-specific.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: No exact blocker; JS/TS Rust toolchain for parse, transform, lint, and resolve.
repo_catalog.why: High-performance JS/TS compiler and tooling stack; strongest fit for source ingestion, AST-based mapping, and spec-compiler-style transforms.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Content corpus, not infrastructure; markdown-to-Anki and PDF deck material.
repo_catalog.why: Useful as curated learning content, but it is not reusable infrastructure for the parent harness.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Needs an LLM stack such as LiteLLM plus PageIndex; strongest when those are already available.
repo_catalog.why: Compiles raw documents into a persistent wiki-style knowledge base, then exposes query, chat, and skill-generation surfaces; strong match for harvest and cartography, but gated by LLM and indexing dependencies.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Needs hookable agent CLIs and workspaces; supported integrations are Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
repo_catalog.why: Agent version control and audit trail with step DAGs, blame, sessions, and hooks; directly relevant to provenance and execution tracing.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Requires native tool-calling models and providers plus its own CLI; MCP is explicitly unsupported.
repo_catalog.why: A full coding agent with hash-anchored edits and AST-native precision; good pattern source, but not reusable infrastructure for the parent harness.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Dashboard-specific YAML and TSX stack that depends on Bruin connections and CLI.
repo_catalog.why: Dashboard-as-code with semantic layers and validation is relevant as a pattern, but the domain and Bruin dependency make it overlap more than it foundations the parent harness.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Requires Java 17 or newer plus a local Temporal Server and CLI.
repo_catalog.why: Samples show durable workflows, Spring Boot integration, metrics and tracing, and Spring AI agents on Temporal; strong for durable execution patterns.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Needs an upstream LLM provider and API key; otherwise it remains a local proxy boundary.
repo_catalog.why: Runtime policy-enforcement proxy that sits between an app and an LLM provider, evaluating RULES.md and blocking, intervening on, or shadowing live traffic.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Exact dependency on Claude Code plugin packaging plus Anthropic API and key.
repo_catalog.why: A Claude Code skill suite for academic research; useful inspiration, but tightly bound to Claude Code's plugin ecosystem.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Exact dependency on the Claude Code plugin marketplace and system.
repo_catalog.why: Marketplace directory for Claude Code plugins; useful as ecosystem reference, but not reusable outside Claude Code.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Exact dependency on OpenCode plus Cursor ACP and cursor-agent integration.
repo_catalog.why: A bridge from OpenCode to Cursor models; strong adapter pattern, but tied to that exact toolchain.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Needs Node 20 or newer and at least one of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, or an OpenRouter key.
repo_catalog.why: Local multi-vendor review orchestrator with MCP server and quorum logic; strong pattern source for durable review flows and observability.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Exact dependency on a local Codex.app installation.
repo_catalog.why: Patches and relaunches the Codex desktop app; useful for app-hook patterns, but locked to that app.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: No exact blocker; self-contained Node-bundled CLI with agent integrations.
repo_catalog.why: Pre-indexed knowledge graph for code structure and call graphs; one of the strongest fits for semantic cartography and source ingestion.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Python-focused static-analysis stack; best when the tranche needs Python sources.
repo_catalog.why: Fast Python type checker and language server; useful for semantic extraction and validation on Python-heavy repositories.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Pre-1 experimental language; explicitly unstable and not production-safe.
repo_catalog.why: Interesting agent-first language experiment, but not a stable reusable substrate for this parent wrapper.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.4+, and supported accelerator and hardware combinations only.
repo_catalog.why: Quantization and runtime library for model memory reduction; useful only as a deployment-layer dependency, not as harness infrastructure.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Locked to RTX 3090-class local-serving setups with Linux, Docker, and the NVIDIA toolkit.
repo_catalog.why: Excellent local-serving recipe set, but it is hardware-specific infrastructure rather than harness logic.

repo_catalog.exact_dependency_or_limit: Needs a supported engine and runtime such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor and writes project scaffolding.
repo_catalog.why: Legacy-to-spec framework with multi-agent discovery, planning, and documentation generation; very relevant to spec-compiler patterns, but engine-gated.

reusable_infrastructure_shortlist.why_now: Best direct fit for semantic cartography and intake ETL because the pre-indexed knowledge graph reduces file-scanning cost and is already agent-facing.
Best direct fit for runtime observability and policy enforcement around the inbox protocol because the proxy boundary matches parent wrapper guardrails.
Best direct fit for provenance, session audit, and durable step tracking; it complements observability and substrate synchronization without broadening into child-runtime claims.
Strong local execution substrate for parent-wrapper automation and test and runtime orchestration, and it aligns with the existing TS-facing surfaces already present in the parent repo.
Strong source-analysis substrate for intake ETL and spec-compiler-style AST work on JS and TS assets.
Strongest reusable pattern source for research harvest and semantic cartography; gated, but structurally aligned with the first subsystem tranche.
